correctness.rationale: The five-step gamma ratio polynomials are exactly expanded and give two order-two branches and three order-one branches. Applying the 5-adic log and the proved complete-block restricted-series sum lemma yields the exact valuation identity on every input residue branch, with unit leading coefficients at all levels. Normalized isometries are onto by finite-residue bijectivity and compactness. The resulting disjoint balls and overlaps determine all output multiplicities. Direct recurrence checker passes 8,190 exact assertions through precision \(5^5\); these finite checks are expressly not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Original 1975 Morita source, Barsky 1977 local analyticity results, Finat's related log-gamma distribution, Li et al.'s general 1-Lipschitz gamma estimate, and later differential-transcendence work were compared by implication. None of the inspected theorem statements gives exact branchwise distance equalities, the 11/25 image, or all output fibers modulo every power of five. Foundational original PDF and a broad textbook are not fully read, so historical priority remains provisional, without a claim of proved uniqueness.
residual_risks: The entire full text of Morita's 1975 original was inaccessible during this comparison, despite available archive metadata; a hidden specialization is possible.
Alain Robert, A Course in p-adic Analysis, sections 35–39, was not directly inspected in full; Proposition 35.3 is quoted in Li et al. 2022 and only gives the weaker Lipschitz property.
Finat 2016 full text and possibly unindexed older gamma-function literature may contain further implicit facts.

value.rationale: The globally exact image and individual residue fibers of a classical p-adic special function are natural analytic-arithmetic invariants. The complete classification reveals nonuniform input compression (two order-two and three order-one branches), a strict \(11/25\) image measure, sevenfold exceptional fibers, and an exact least period at all finite precisions. These are not routine consequences of continuity or a generic Lipschitz bound; they supply local representability data useful in gamma-value congruences.
